WITH cons AS (
  SELECT c.segment,
         SUBSTR(y.date,1,4) AS yr,
         SUM(y.consumption) AS total_consumption
  FROM customers c
  JOIN yearmonth y ON c.customerid = y.customerid
  WHERE c.currency = 'EUR'
    AND SUBSTR(y.date,1,4) IN ('2012','2013')
  GROUP BY c.segment, SUBSTR(y.date,1,4)
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT segment,
         MAX(CASE WHEN yr = '2012' THEN total_consumption END) AS c2012,
         MAX(CASE WHEN yr = '2013' THEN total_consumption END) AS c2013
  FROM cons
  GROUP BY segment
)
SELECT segment,
       (c2013 - c2012) AS increase,
       CAST((c2013 - c2012) AS REAL) * 100 / c2013 AS pct_increase
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY pct_increase DESC;
answer: Among SME, LAM and KAM customers paying in EUR, the LAM segment had the biggest percentage increase in consumption from 2012 to 2013, while the SME segment had the lowest (smallest, possibly negative) percentage increase.
assumptions: Currency = 'EUR' filter is applied on the customers table to select consumption paid in EUR
Year is derived from the first 4 characters of the date string in yearmonth
Percentage increase formula follows the hint exactly: (2013-2012)/2013*100
